selection: second round after a failed first round

neighbours.label: The adjective that posits an unseen agent: unseen, invisible, unknown, undetected, mysterious, before a force, hand or substance; other adjectives before such nouns stay low
fire: Sailors spoke of an unseen current dragging the boats north.
Old texts describe an invisible fluid that fills the heavens.
Some unknown agent had been souring the village wells.
Researchers posit an undetected planet beyond the outer belt.
A mysterious force seemed to pull the needle aside.
Priests told of invisible powers that ruled the harvest.
An unseen hand had moved the markers overnight.
Doctors blamed some unknown factor in the water.
quiet: Sailors spoke of a strong current dragging the boats north.
Old texts describe a golden chariot that crosses the heavens.
Some careless farmer had been fouling the village wells.
Researchers suspect a frozen planet beyond the outer belt.
A heavy magnet seemed to pull the needle aside.
Priests told of cruel kings who ruled the harvest.
A tired clerk had moved the markers overnight.
Doctors blamed some rusty pipe in the water.

notes: Second round. Round 1 failed because ' a' after 'think' or 'suspect' read 0.31 in near misses; a probe repeated that (' a' 0.26-0.31). Near misses here keep one such frame, and the rest use other adjectives.
